properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 4 at 9:58PM CDT until October 5 at 12:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Alabama, including the following
areas, Baldwin Central, Baldwin Coastal, Baldwin Inland, Mobile
Central, Mobile Coastal and Mobile Inland and northwest Florida,
including the following areas, Escambia Coastal, Escambia Inland,
Okaloosa Coastal, Okaloosa Inland, Santa Rosa Coastal and Santa
Rosa Inland.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional heavy rainfall will be possible through the morning
hours. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected
with locally higher amounts of up to 5 inches possible. This may
lead to flash flooding, especially in urban and poor drainage
areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 4 at 9:53PM CDT until October 4 at 11:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Pensacola FL to Pascagoula MS out 20 NM...
Pensacola Bay Area including Santa Rosa Sound...
Perdido Bay Area...

* Until 1100 PM CDT.

* At 952 PM CDT, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Arnica Bay, or near Perdido Pass,
moving northeast at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Arnica Bay, Orange Beach, Big Lagoon, Pensacola Pass, Perdido Bay,
Fort Pickens, and Perdido Pass.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 4 at 7:33PM PDT until October 8 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves are expected
due to elevated surf of 3 to 6 feet. Abnormally high morning and
evening tides of 6.5 to 7 ft are expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Most
susceptible areas will be Long Beach and Avalon Harbor Tuesday
and Wednesday. Then, Malibu to Ventura Wednesday through
Friday.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
morning and evening high tides, including over beach parking
lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion
is possible to likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a moderate chance that an
upgrade to Coastal Flood Advisory and/or High Surf Advisory
will be needed. These products will likely need to be extended
into the weekend.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 4 at 9:17PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
At 916 PM CDT...A cluster of strong thunderstorms was located 21 nm
south of Gulf Shores Beach...moving east at 15 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Navarre Beach, Pensacola Beach, Oriskany Reef, Pensacola Pass, and
Perdido Pass.

The primary threats from this storm are wind gusts up to 30 knots...
locally higher waves...and heavy downpours. Boaters should consider
seeking safe harbor until this storm has passed.

Weather conditions support the development of waterspouts.
Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally hazardous
waves and seas. If a waterspout is sighted...seek safe harbor
immediately.
